literal: Like women of single-minded chastity, greatness also, if one conducts oneself maintaining oneself, exists.
translation: Just like women of single-minded chastity, greatness exists only when a person guards and conducts themselves with self-discipline.
modern: ஒருமைப்பாடு உடைய கற்புடைய பெண்களைப் போல, பெருமை என்னும் பண்பும் ஒருவன் தன்னைத் தானே காத்துக் கொண்டு ஒழுக்கத்தோடு வாழ்ந்தால் தான் நிலைபெற்று இருக்கும்.
explanation: This couplet compares the preservation of personal greatness to the single-minded chastity of virtuous women. The word 'orumaic' refers to singleness of mind, which represents unwavering fidelity and self-control. The poet explains that greatness is not a permanent birthright; it only exists if a person actively guards their own character and conducts themselves with discipline. Just as a chaste woman protects her virtue, an individual must constantly guard their integrity to maintain true greatness.
